headline: Showers tonight, then a wet, windy week with coastal flooding Monday and heavy rain midweek.
summary: An upper-level low, a cold low-pressure system high in the atmosphere, drifts offshore and merges into a broad Pacific dip in the winds on Monday, opening the door to a series of storms. Tonight brings light rain to the lowlands and snow showers to the mountains. Monday and Tuesday turn wetter and windier, with gusty southeast winds on the coast and possible coastal flooding at Monday morning's high tide in Grays Harbor County. Wednesday into Thursday looks wettest, with heavy rain over the Olympics. Highs stay near 50, and winds and high surf persist into the weekend. Forecasters are confident in a wet, windy week but unsure how strong the midweek low will be or how widespread its gales will get.
changes: The main coastal flooding concern moved from midweek to Monday morning's high tide, and a coastal flood warning was issued for the Grays Harbor coast by the afternoon. Wind products for the outer coast were also upgraded from watches to warnings for Monday into Tuesday.
